findings.problem: The candidate isolates the preparatory left turn as a standalone stage with no independent destination or useful local objective. The source couples the turn to the subsequent stair ascent; the cut adds a task boundary without exposing a separately completed navigation goal.
findings.execution_consequence: The navigator receives an orientation-only micro-goal with no distinct destination, creating an unnecessary subtask transition before the stair approach and weakening focus on the coupled turn-and-climb leg.
